name: Plastic
steps: Empty the container and rinse out any food or liquid.
Check the recycling symbol and number on the bottom (1 to 7).
Remove the cap and label if possible, and crush the bottle to save space.
Keep it dry and put it in the blue bin or the nearest plastic collection point.
dos: Rinse bottles and containers before recycling
Keep plastic items with numbers 1, 2, and 5 separate if your local centre asks for it
Flatten bottles to save space
donts: Do not put greasy or food-stained plastic in the bin
Do not burn plastic waste
Do not put thermocol or plastic bags in the same bin without checking

name: Paper
steps: Remove staples, paper clips, and plastic windows from envelopes.
Keep the paper dry and clean.
Stack newspapers, notebooks, and office paper together.
Put it in the blue bin or give it to a paper scrap dealer.
dos: Keep paper dry, because wet paper cannot be recycled
Shred confidential documents before recycling
Give old newspapers and magazines to a scrap dealer
donts: Do not recycle greasy or food-stained paper
Do not include wax-coated paper or tissues
Do not put paper in the wet (green) bin

name: Glass
steps: Empty the bottle or jar and rinse it.
Remove the metal lid or cork (lids go with metal).
Keep whole bottles and jars separate from broken glass.
Wrap broken glass in newspaper and mark it clearly before handing it over.
dos: Rinse glass bottles and jars
Keep glass colours separate if the centre asks (clear, green, brown)
Wrap broken glass safely
donts: Do not put mirrors, window glass, or light bulbs in glass recycling
Do not put ceramics or crockery in glass recycling
Do not leave broken glass loose in the dustbin

name: E-waste
steps: Back up your data, then delete personal information from the device.
Remove the battery if it is easy to take out (see the Battery guide).
Keep cables and accessories together with the device.
Take it to an authorised e-waste collection point or a certified recycler.
dos: Wipe personal data before handing over a device
Take e-waste only to authorised collection points
Keep chargers and cables with the device
donts: Do not throw e-waste in the dustbin
Do not burn or break electronics to get parts
Do not give old devices to unauthorised scrap sellers without checking

name: Battery
steps: Stop using the battery if it is swollen, leaking, or damaged.
Tape the terminals (+ and -) with insulating tape to prevent short circuits.
Store it in a dry place in a separate box.
Drop it at a battery collection box or an e-waste collection point.
dos: Tape the terminals of every battery
Keep used batteries in a separate, dry container
Ask shops that sell batteries about take-back programmes
donts: Never throw batteries in the dustbin
Do not heat, puncture, or crush batteries
Do not keep damaged or leaking batteries in your home

name: Metal
steps: Empty cans and tins and rinse them out.
Crush or flatten cans to save space, if safe to do so.
Keep aluminium and steel items together if the centre separates them.
Give metal scrap to a metal scrap dealer or the nearest collection point.
dos: Rinse food cans before recycling
Crush cans to save space
Sell or give large metal scrap to registered dealers
donts: Do not put aerosol cans with pressure left in the bin
Do not put metal items with sharp edges loose in the bin without wrapping
Do not mix metal with wet food waste

name: Cardboard
steps: Remove tape, labels, and plastic packaging from the box.
Flatten the box completely.
Keep it dry, because wet cardboard loses its value.
Put it in the blue bin or give it to a scrap dealer.
dos: Flatten boxes before recycling
Remove tape and plastic from boxes
Keep cardboard dry
donts: Do not recycle waxed or heavily greasy cardboard (such as pizza boxes with grease)
Do not put cardboard in the wet (green) bin
Do not leave wet cardboard outside

name: Food Waste (Compost)
steps: Separate vegetable peels, fruit scraps, tea leaves, and leftover cooked food.
Drain liquids from the food waste.
Keep it in the green bin, or start a small home compost pit or bin.
Remove plastic packaging before putting it in the compost.
dos: Use the green bin for wet waste
Drain liquids before putting food in the bin
Chop large pieces to speed up composting
donts: Do not put plastic bags or packaging in compost
Do not put oil, ghee, or cooking fat in the compost bin
Do not put dry waste like paper or glass in the green bin
